options.title: What Carries Your Internet Across the Ocean Floor?
options.first_line: The video on your phone just crossed an ocean. So what carried it across the seabed?
options.first_frame: A glowing phone playing a video on a dark stage, a beam of light already shooting out of it and down through a cut-away beach into the dark seabed.

options.title: How Does a Cable Thinner Than a Hose Carry the Internet?
options.first_line: This cable on the ocean floor is about as wide as a garden hose. How does the internet fit inside it?
options.first_frame: A dark cable lying across the lit seabed, the camera already sliding along it as a pulse of light races inside, a garden hose fading in beside it at the same width.

options.title: Why Doesn't the Internet Die When a Seabed Cable Snaps?
options.first_line: Somewhere on the seabed, a ship's anchor is dragging across an internet cable. Why don't you notice?
options.first_frame: A huge anchor already scraping along the dark seabed towards a glowing cable, sand rising behind it, the camera pushing in.

why: A garden hose beside the cable makes the size visible with the sound off and raises a real 'how is that possible?' that only the video answers, while A's answer (a cable) is guessable and C's anchor is tension without a picture of the viewer's own internet.
